why: On 2026-09-06 one x402 change left FOUR derived artefacts stale at once — the byte-identical agent-card alias, the JWS signing input, the a2a census (our_agent.skills 6 against the card's 7), and public/llms.txt (missing 13 lines its own template already carried). Every one had a working test, every test went red, and they were found one at a time over an hour because nothing in the repo records which artefacts derive from what. This file is that record; scripts/producers-gate.mjs is the check that re-runs each producer and fails if any output moves.
rule: An entry means: run `cmd`, and `outputs` must not change. If they change, the source moved and the artefact was not re-produced. Fix by running the producer, never by editing the output — every one of these files is generated. A producer may declare `volatile`: substrings whose lines are ignored when comparing, for fields like a build date that legitimately move on every run. Declaring one is a claim that the field carries no meaning a reader would act on — use it sparingly.
seeded_by: TUI-6, 2026-09-06, with producers it verified by running them. Not exhaustive: extend it. An absent producer is an unguarded artefact, not a safe one.

producers.note: JCS(card minus signatures) prepared for GHA OIDC. A stale input means signing bytes nobody serves.
Snapshot of App.tsx routes. link-gate reads it to know what the app serves.
ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING in the output: a splat placed early bills every later rule to the 100-rule dynamic budget.

Must run AFTER redirects: it reconciles against public/_redirects. lastmod is stamped with the build date, so it moves every day; it is declared volatile and excluded from the drift comparison. Everything else in the file must be stable.

Reads the LIVE board, so a board change moves the output legitimately. The gate reports these separately and does not fail on them — scripts/llms-txt.mjs --check is the one that adjudicates, and it already runs in pr-gates.
